issues.description: Removed valid test case proves the old grammar accepted mixed ADD/DROP in one statement; new grammar silently regresses it
issues.detail: The deleted fixture `ALTER TABLE ... ADD column_b ... CONSTRAINT exb_unique UNIQUE, DROP COLUMN column_a, DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS column_c` is valid TSQL per MS docs. The new OneOf structure cannot parse a mixed ADD-then-DROP in a single statement. The PR removes the test rather than supporting it. That is a regression dressed up as cleanup. Either keep the case working or document explicitly why it is being dropped.

issues.description: THREE-PATCHES: four unrelated parser changes shipped as one diff
issues.detail: Table-var indexes, CREATE LOGIN options, negative identity seed, and ALTER TABLE DROP restructuring are four independent features touching different grammars. When one of them regresses in six months, bisect lands on a commit that did four things. Split: one patch per feature, each with its own fixture. The commit message even enumerates them as bullets, which is the tell.

issues.description: SignedSegmentGrammar on the increment allows nonsense like IDENTITY(1, -1)
issues.detail: The diff adds optional `SignedSegmentGrammar` before BOTH numerics in the identity bracket. TSQL allows a negative seed; the increment must be a non-zero integer but in practice SQL Server accepts negative increments too, so this may be fine. However, the change is silently permissive without a fixture proving negative increment was the intent. Add a test for `IDENTITY(-5, 1)` and state whether negative increment is intentional.

issues.description: DEFAULT_LANGUAGE now accepts NumericLiteralSegment with no justification in the PR text
issues.detail: The PR description says `DEFAULT_LANGUAGE` should accept a non-quoted identifier. The diff also adds `NumericLiteralSegment` to the OneOf. That is an undocumented scope creep inside a patch already doing four things. Either the commit message should mention the language-id case (e.g. `DEFAULT_LANGUAGE=1033`) with a fixture, or drop the NumericLiteralSegment.

issues.description: DROP CONSTRAINT grammar makes CONSTRAINT keyword optional inside the Delimited - shape is fragile
issues.detail: The inner `Sequence(Sequence("CONSTRAINT", IfExistsGrammar, optional=True), ObjectReferenceSegment)` means a bare object reference parses as a DROP target with no CONSTRAINT keyword. That is not valid TSQL after `ALTER TABLE ... DROP`. Tighten: CONSTRAINT keyword should be required on each delimited item (the fixture shows it appearing on every item anyway).

issues.description: Outer OneOf replaces Delimited(OneOf(...)) - lost the ability to chain table options
issues.detail: The old grammar wrapped everything in `Delimited(OneOf(...))` so multiple comma-separated alter actions could chain. The new grammar is bare `OneOf(...)`. Combined with the deleted mixed test case, this confirms loss of multi-action ALTER TABLE support. If that was intentional, say so in the commit message; if not, this is wrong-shape.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. Four unrelated features in one diff — table-var indexes, CREATE LOGIN options, negative identity seeds, and ALTER TABLE DROP restructuring — should be three or four patches so bisect can do its job later. The real concern is the deleted alter_table fixture: a previously-parsing mixed ADD/DROP statement now fails because the wrapping `Delimited(OneOf(...))` became a bare `OneOf(...)`. That is a regression hidden by deleting the test that would have caught it. Smaller issues: DEFAULT_LANGUAGE silently gained NumericLiteralSegment with no fixture or mention, and the DROP CONSTRAINT inner sequence makes the CONSTRAINT keyword optional in a way that accepts invalid TSQL. Split the patch, restore or explicitly justify dropping the mixed-action case, and add fixtures for every grammar broadening.
